An attacker can change the SQL syntax if the name is interpolated into a quoted SQL string without correctly escaping it. Passing the name separately as a bound parameter keeps it data. Doubling single quotes also keeps them within a SQLite string literal. A formatted SQL string is safe for this target if only trusted structure is formatted and the name remains bound. Mentally use a name containing a single quote and SQL syntax. If it stays a single literal value through the actual execution call, choose not_vulnerable_for_target. If it can alter the SQL expression, choose vulnerable.

Target category: sql_injection
